title: Jersey City Home Energy Rebates 2026: PSE&G Heat Pump, Thermostat and Free Help
desc: Home energy rebates in Jersey City for 2026: PSE&G heat pump rebates up to $10,000, smart thermostat and appliance rebates, free weatherization, and what renters and condo owners can use.
h1: Home Energy Rebates in Jersey City
lead: Jersey City has more new buildings than most New Jersey cities, a lot of renters and a high share of electric heat. PSE&G is the utility, and its heat pump rebates are written for people who own a house of up to four homes. Many Jersey City households live in a bigger building, so the rebates they can use are different. This page shows both paths, with the numbers we read on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open in Jersey City in 2026
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page. PSE&G can change or end its programs without notice.

cards.title: Heat pump that replaces gas, oil or propane
cards.note: For owners of houses of one to four units. Income-qualified homes can get up to $12,000. The rules are the same as in Newark.

cards.title: Standard heat pump
cards.note: Instant rebate by efficiency tier, plus $300 if you are income-qualified. The owner of the home applies through a participating contractor.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: Up to $100 after you buy, $60 with a heating and cooling job, or free from a Whole Home Energy Assessment. See the thermostat guide.

cards.title: Whole Home Energy Assessment
cards.note: A one-hour visit that can leave free products behind, from LED bulbs to a smart thermostat.

cards.title: Appliance rebates
cards.note: Induction cooktop $250, electric dryer up to $300, dishwasher $30 and more. See the appliance guide.

cards.title: Electric car charger
cards.note: PSE&G pays for charger setup on a single residential meter. See the electric car guide.

cards.title: PSE&G Home Weatherization
cards.note: For households between 250% and 400% of the poverty level, in moderate-income areas or in overburdened communities.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D credits
cards.note: No federal credit applies to work done after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: The full list, with dates, is on our PSE&G rebates page.
sections: The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 135,231 homes in Jersey City, 125,223 of them someone's usual home. About 29.8% were built in 2000 or later, the highest share of our four New Jersey cities, and only 55.9% were built before 1980. Detached houses are just 7.3% of the total and attached houses 7.1%. Buildings with two to four homes are 31.5%. The rest, a little over half, are in larger buildings or other housing types.

Renters live in 72.1% of Jersey City homes and owners in 27.9%. PSE&G's heat pump program asks for the owner of the house, and its decarbonization rules cover single-family and attached homes of one to four units. If you own a three-family house, you are covered. If you own a condo unit in a large building, the rules do not clearly say, so call PSE&G at 1-855-846-2895 and ask before you hire anyone. Renters can use the free assessment and the appliance rebates, and can show the owner the heat pump page.

Electricity heats 31.7% of Jersey City homes, the highest share among our PSE&G cities. Utility gas heats 60.9%, bottled gas 2.0% and fuel oil 2.6%. For an electric-heat home, the standard instant rebate of $300 to $600 applies, and the savings come from using less electricity: a heat pump moves heat rather than making it. The large replacement rebate is for gas, oil and propane homes.

Many Jersey City homes are newer than the average New Jersey home, so insulation is often better than in a 1930s building. That can make a heat pump easier to size. Still, new construction is not eligible for PSE&G's rebates, so a home that was just built is out. Ask the seller or the building manager how old the building is and when the heating system went in.

The free Whole Home Energy Assessment is the lowest-risk first step for an apartment or a house. The visit takes about an hour and PSE&G can install a smart thermostat and small items at no cost, while supplies last. If you earn between 250% and 400% of the federal poverty level, live in a moderate-income area or an overburdened community, PSE&G Home Weatherization covers insulation and sealing work too. Below 250%, the state's Comfort Partners program applies.
claim_heading: How to get started in Jersey City
claim_steps: Check that PSE&G is your electric company.
Find out who owns the home or unit where the work would be done.
Book the free Whole Home Energy Assessment or call 1-855-846-2895 for a participating contractor.
Ask for a written quote that shows each rebate line.
Keep invoices, model numbers and photos.
faq: Yes. Jersey City appears in Hudson County on PSE&G's official service territory list, for both electric and gas.
I own a condo. Can I get a heat pump rebate?
The rules cover houses of one to four units that you own. For a unit in a larger building, ask PSE&G before you buy.
Yes. Renters can use appliance rebates and the free assessment, and income-qualified households can use free weatherization.
The standard heat pump rebate of $300 to $600, plus $300 more for income-qualified homes.
Is there a federal tax credit?
No. The 25C and 25D credits ended for work done after December 31, 2025.
